question: What is the meaning of compatibility of components in relation to remanufacturing?
description:
The compatibility of components is essential for optimizing the use of existing parts and materials, enabling re­
manufacturers to reduce costs and minimize the need for new materials by understanding which components can be interchanged or updated. 
This approach supports efficient and effective remanufacturing processes.

3.2. Benefits of DPPs for remanufacturing strategies
DPPs can become essential in remanufacturing by providing detailed 
product and component information. The DPPs can offer different 
specifications, including materials, dimensions, design files, and 
manufacturing processes, which are important for identifying and 
assessing products for remanufacturing (Berger et al., 2023b; Kur­
ilova-Palisaitiene et al., 2018). Additionally, DPPs facilitate efficient 
remanufacturing by including the history of previous repairs, re­
furbishments, and modifications, along with component life cycle data 
and compatibility information, thus reducing uncertainties in the 
remanufacturing process (Gallina et al., 2022; Paterson et al., 2017). 
DPPs can also enable predictive maintenance, utilizing operational data 
and maintenance records to predict potential failures. This approach 
reduces the complexity of maintenance activities and extends the 
products’ life (Rehman Khan et al., 2022). Structured data governance is 
central to enhancing the utility and reliability of information within 
DPPs for predictive maintenance and efficient remanufacturing, show­
casing the importance of managing data to support CE strategies effec­
tively (Ducuing and Reich, 2023). DPPs also assist in the reusability 
assessment of components by providing detailed disassembly in­
structions and information on materials, thereby ensuring efficient and 
safe reuse practices (Rusch et al., 2022). Moreover, sharing usage and 
maintenance data through DPPs enables informed choices among 
stakeholders, contributing to sustainable product use and maintenance 
practices, which align with the strategies of the CE (Walden et al., 2021).
3.2.1. Data needs for remanufacturing strategies
The remanufacturing strategy is supported by integrating various 
data points, each contributing to the efficiency and effectiveness of 
remanufacturing processes. Detailed product specifications are funda­
mental to any remanufacturing effort, providing necessary information 
on product design, materials, and components required for remanu­
facturing processes to meet the required quality standards and technical 
parameters, ensuring consistency and reliability (Wang et al., 2021). 
The history of previous repair and remanufacturing offers insights into a 
product’s interventions, allowing remanufacturers to assess the viability 
of further remanufacturing and develop effective strategies for future 
cycles (Liu et al., 2023). The compatibility of components is essential for 
optimizing the use of existing parts and materials, enabling re­
manufacturers to reduce costs and minimize the need for new materials 
by understanding which components can be interchanged or updated 
(Remery et al., 2012). Estimating the remaining lifetime of products and 
components allows for strategic planning of remanufacturing activities, 
prioritizing products most suitable for remanufacturing based on their 
continued use potential (Hu et al., 2014). Continuous conditional 
monitoring provides real-time data for informing remanufacturing de­
cisions, enabling the early identification of wear and tear to preserve 
product value by scheduling remanufacturing before significant degra­
dation (Zhang, M. et al., 2022). Access to detailed disassembly in­
structions reduces the resources required to disassemble products, 
ensuring components are recovered safely and intact for remanu­
facturing (Soh et al., 2014). Predicting the return of products for 
remanufacturing is important for better planning and resource alloca­
tion, helping manage inventory, anticipating material availability, and 
ensuring a steady supply of products for remanufacturing (Goltsos et al., 
2019).
3.3. Benefits of DPPs for recycle strategies
DPPs enhance recycling efficiency by tracking product material 
composition and recyclability.
